problem:
Calculate the value of 
$\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & -3 & -1 \\ 1 & 4 & -2 & -3 \\ -2 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}|.$

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left of ${a}_{44}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4\times 4$ determinant to a $3\times 3$ determinant.*

activity_context.topic_title: Finding Determinants Using Row and Column Operations

examples.knowledge_point: Computing 4x4 Determinants Using Row and Column Operations
examples.problem:
Calculate the value of 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14058571/assets/9cb26049b5e3d06f9ef9e07ce617042166330b1eddb84063d7970799ebf6d8e5.png)

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of $a_{31}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4 \times 4$ determinant to a $3 \times 3$ determinant.*
examples.worked_solution:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the right of $a_{31}=1$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (or column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -4 & -2 & 6 \\ 1 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+3{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+(-3){C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -3 & -5 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -3 & -5 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+1}|\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & -5 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & -5 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -3 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =4(11-3) \\  & =32.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -4 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 & -2 \\ 2 & -2 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{22}$ equal to zero.*
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{22}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -4 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 & -2 \\ 2 & -2 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+2{C}_{2} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+3{C}_{2} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+(-4){C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 & -7 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 2 & 10 & -10 \\ -2 & -2 & -4 & 13\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 & -7 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 2 & 10 & -10 \\ -2 & -2 & -4 & 13\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}-3 & -7 & 5 \\ 5 & 10 & -10 \\ -2 & -4 & 13\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & -7 & 5 \\ 5 & 10 & -10 \\ -2 & -4 & 13\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
